title: Request Weave Workbench — notes and fast proposals
body:
Executive snapshot:
- Quick synthesis of customer asks received 2027-04 → 2027-05 across frontline CS and SRE channels. Focus: runtime fragility, kv-cache visibility, rollout controls, and cost surprises from burst workloads.

Top-line themes (high signal):
1) kv-cache visibility and per-customer cache metrics: multiple customers (Acme Health, Kumo AI) report inability to reason about cache hit patterns; leads them to disable caching and pay 2x in tokens.
2) Latency cliffs during autoscale/placement decisions: Retailio and one startup reported 200–400ms p99 spikes when routing to different capacity tiers.
3) Model fallback quality tradeoffs: Customers want a declarative fallback policy that bounds quality loss (not just latency/cost).
4) Billing surprises for replays and retries: developers confused about which tokens are charged when system retries short-circuited requests.

Representative customer quotes (raw):
- "We turned off cache because we couldn't explain the odd hallucination frequency spikes — but cost doubled." — Eng lead, Acme Health.
- "During a busy hour our p95 was fine but p99 went to the moon; support said it's autoscale. We need to own the fallback behavior." — Platform PM, Retailio.
- "We need an easy knob to say 'fall back only if similarity score < X' — otherwise fallback is useless for us." — ML engineer, Kumo AI.

Raw asks (short):
- per-customer kv cache hit/miss timeline + top prefixes evicted
- per-route rollout policy option: 'strict-quality-budget' with thresholding
- clearer token billing flow for retries/replays with examples in Console
- quick toggle for 'sticky placement' to avoid cross-pool hops for warm sessions
- instrumented canary that runs post-rollout deterministic evals on a small prompt set

Micro-proposals (low-effort / fast iterations):
A. KV-cache playback sample (2–3 engineer days)
- Small API surface: /admin/cache/export?customer_id=... returns top-100 prefixes (hashed) + hit-rate time series (1m granularity).
- UI: quick chart in Console under per-customer route.
- Benefit: unblocks root-cause for ~40% of cache-related asks.
- Risks: privacy of prefixes -> transmission as hashed + sampled.

B. 'Fallback quality guard' toggle (1 sprint frontend + 1 sprint backend)
- New rollout policy field: quality_guard = {enabled: true, threshold: 0.75}
- Backend returns metadata (fallback_reason, score_before, score_after) for first 50 tokens so customers can audit.
- Minimal opt-in via Console.

C. Billing explain docs + sample traces (docs + small UI badge)
- Doc page with 3 canonical scenarios: retry vs replay vs client-side resend.
- Console: show billed_tokens_breakdown per request when expanded.

D. Sticky placement experiment (prototype 2 weeks)
- Per-session affinity flag assigned at route level. If set, router prefers same pool for N minutes.
- Quick metric: measure p99 reduction in pilot customer over 2 weeks.

Cost / latency impact heuristics (very rough):
- KV-cache playback endpoint: infra cost ~ $500/month for 100 customers storing sampled timelines; benefit: savings for customers who re-enable caches could be 15–35% token savings.
- Fallback-quality guard: small CPU overhead (score computation) + metadata tokens; negligible infra costs; high customer value.
- Sticky placement: could increase cold-start resource holding; need guardrails (time-to-live, max-affinity-sessions).

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Data privacy: what hashing and retention policy is acceptable for exporting prefixes? Legal needs to sign off.
- How to compute a standard 'quality score' across model families? Should be model-agnostic metric (e.g., similarity to reference, or evalset score).
- Billing UX: do we show estimated cost-savings from suggested toggles? Who owns the copy for docs? (CS + Docs + Billing).

Action items (owners tentative):
- Maya: draft Confluence page for KV export privacy approach — due 2027-05-20.
- Priya: coordinate a small pilot with Retailio for sticky placement — ask for two routes and 2-week pilot — due 2027-05-24.
- Liam: spike prototype of fallback-quality guard on staging (2 dev days), measure CPU & latency overheads — due 2027-05-21.
- Samir: create draft billing examples and map to current token accounting logic — due 2027-05-22.

Quick heuristics for triage (for product/eng prioritization):
- If ask reduces >10% token spend for an enterprise customer or prevents an outage class (latency cliff), mark P0.
- If ask is clearly a visibility/observability win with <2 engineer-weeks cost, mark P1 and push to next sprint.
- If ask is cosmetic/help-text only, bucket P3.

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets for 2027-05-19 sync with Eng-Serving-Runtime:
- Bring one concrete timeline for KV export privacy options (hashing+salt+retention).
- Ask SRE about placing affinity TTL and how that would interfere with autoscaler signals.
- Request quick experiment: run sticky placement on a small subset of sessions for 48h and capture p95/p99 deltas.

Appendix — quick pilot candidate list (why chosen):
- Retailio: p99 spikes are business-visible; willing to be early adopter; route has stable traffic shape.
- Kumo AI: active ML team; wants fallback-quality guard; quick to evaluate.
- Acme Health: sensitive prefixes (PHI) — good test for hashed-prefix UX + privacy work.

End notes: This is intentionally a workbench doc — choppy items, TODOs, and half-formed proposals. Use this as input for the CS x Eng runbook meeting and for a short pilot plan. Will convert high-confidence items into product stories if engineering scope is clean.

-- Maya (notes)
